learning: Expect the wider span to remove the line loss near ±0.05 m. Watch for added centre-noise and for kp being too high, which would show as higher steering_oscillation.
notes: Adopts the wider seven-sensor span (±0.06 m, 16 mm footprints) and 0.6 kg mass from the Builder's proposal. Weights are rescaled to fit ±2 and kp is raised to keep steering gain comparable, based on iteration 0's off-track failure at max_error ≈ 0.063 m.
rationale: Iteration 0 failed on all 60 trials: every run went off track, with about one line-loss event each and progress of 0.09 to 0.21. Max error was about 0.063 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and the drift began right after the line was lost near ±0.04 m. Body width cannot widen that limit, so the fix has to come from sensing. I adopt the Builder's proposed geometry as written: seven sensors at 0.02 m spacing spanning ±0.06 m, 16 mm footprints (about 14 mm gaps, smaller than the 25 mm tape), mass 0.6 kg, and unchanged wheel track, wheel radius and body. Because the span is wider, the weights are rescaled to 2/0.06 × x (about 33.3 × x, clipped to ±2) so that the signal is still a lateral-offset estimate within the ±2 weight limit. The old signal scale was 50 per metre, so the new one is about 0.67 times as large. To keep the same effective steering gain I raise kp from 4.5 to 6.0 (close to 4.5 × 50/33.3 ≈ 6.75, slightly lower to limit noise at the centre, where the larger footprint may add signal jitter). A lighter body has less yaw inertia, so kd rises only a little to 0.3 to damp the faster response, and ki stays small at 0.05. base_speed stays at 1.8 and line_loss stays at last_direction, since the loss still occurs at bend edges. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and max_error held below 0.06 m. This is an expectation, not a measured result. Note: the Builder's requested sum-of-readings and line-loss-step measurements are not in the allowed observation set, so I request the closest allowed measurements.
